note: Descriptive strategy mechanics only. No p-values: regime windows are outside every correction family in this study, by design. Backfills the window omitted from the first version of BRIEF.md.

declared.rationale: Decomposition component 1/3 of the note's p.2 headline rule: the band-touch condition alone, with the 200MA regime gate removed. Exit is the mid-band (SMA20) touch, i.e. 'reversion to the mean achieved' -- this doubles as the band-touch-as-exit test from note p.9, using the middle band as the (partial) reversion target.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.2 headline rule, decomposed: band-touch component alone

declared.rationale: Decomposition component 2/3 of the note's p.2 headline rule: the 200MA regime gate alone, with the band-touch condition removed. Same expression as the trend-ma stream's regime_filter_standalone and the prior study's momentum_persistence, run here as this stream's own decomposition baseline, not claimed as a fresh replication.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.2 headline rule, decomposed: 200MA gate alone

declared.rationale: Decomposition component 3/3, and the note's headline rule verbatim (p.2): 'IF price > 200 MA AND price < lower BB THEN Buy'. This is the exact expression behind the smoke-test numbers this stream exists to reproduce and extend (SPY edge +0.134, n_indep=87, p=0.0075; QQQ edge +0.099, n_indep=63, p=0.153 -- both from a 2-test family, re-corrected here across the full 8x5 family). Exit uses the opposite (upper) band as the full mean-reversion target, the note p.9 band-touch-exit concept applied to the headline rule itself.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.2, headline entry logic, verbatim

declared.rationale: note p.5 z-score entry band, |0.5| < z < |2|, oversold/long construction: price is moderately below its 20-day mean (more than half a band-half-width, less than a full band-half-width) -- the note's 'stretched rubber band, likely to snap back' zone. Exit at the mid-band, i.e. the z=0 line.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.5, z-score banded entry |0.5| < z < |2|

declared.rationale: note p.5's hard-stop reasoning, tested as an empirical claim rather than wired in as a position-management stop (the DSL's stop_loss_pct is a price-percentage field, not a z-score-conditioned one, so the literal 'exit the position if z exceeds 3' mechanism is not directly expressible -- see 'what this cannot express'). Same direction, exit, horizon and holding cap as zscore_oversold_band, differing only in how far below the mean the entry requires: if the note's reasoning holds (extreme deviation is trend, not a stretched rubber band), this entry's edge should be weaker than, not stronger than, the moderate band's.
declared.falsifies_if: extreme-deviation (z<-3) entries do not show a weaker 20-bar edge than the moderate band (zscore_oversold_band) -- if the edges are equal or the extreme entry is stronger, the note's stop-out reasoning is not supported
declared.source: note p.5, hard stop at |z| > 3 ('large deviation means a strong trend, not a stretched rubber band')

declared.rationale: note p.5: bandwidth < 5% => compression / consolidating regime, i.e. a breakout is coming. Uses the note's own 5% threshold on (upper-lower)/mid -- NOT the prior study's volatility_contraction template, which used (upper-lower) < close*0.04, a 4% threshold on a DIFFERENT denominator (close, not the mid band). That discrepancy is reported, not silently reconciled. The note's claim is direction-agnostic (a breakout can go either way); the harness's hit-rate statistic is not, so this idea tests only the directional half of the claim and the report reads median forward return alongside hit rate to keep that limitation visible rather than overclaiming a directional finding.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.5, BB bandwidth < 5% => compression/consolidating

declared.rationale: note p.5: bandwidth > 15% => high-volatility trending regime. Same directional-statistic caveat as bb_bandwidth_compression: 'trending' does not itself specify up or down, so this tests whether wide-band conditions on this long-biased universe skew up, alongside the strategy mechanics' own volatility metric.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.5, BB bandwidth > 15% => high-volatility trending regime

declared.rationale: note p.5 names both BOLL(20,2) and BOLL(50,2). 50-period analogue of bb_lower_only (same exit/horizon/direction/holding-cap shape) so the two are directly comparable: does the band-touch effect, such as it is, depend on lookback length?
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.5, 'BOLL(20,2)' and 'BOLL(50,2)' both named

declared.rationale: note p.6: MACD line crossing above its own signal line (EMA9 of the MACD line) is the canonical MACD entry trigger. Tested as its own idea, distinct from the zero-line cross -- the note conflates the two, they are not the same signal.
declared.falsifies_if: 10-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.6 MACD signal-line crossover

declared.rationale: note p.6: 'zero line = the momentum midpoint'. MACD crossing zero means EMA12 has just overtaken EMA26 outright -- a coarser, later trigger than the signal-line cross, tested separately at the identical horizon.
declared.falsifies_if: 10-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.6 MACD zero-line cross

declared.rationale: Matched comparator for the note's own claim (p.6, verbatim): 'MACD crossover is faster but more falsy than MA crossover.' Matched on EMA(10)/EMA(20) rather than SMA(5)/SMA(20) because MACD is itself built from two EMAs (12,26); holding the smoothing family constant isolates the actual mechanical difference this claim is about -- crossing two EMAs directly vs. crossing the EMA12-EMA26 difference against its own EMA9-smoothed signal line -- rather than also changing SMA-vs-EMA responsiveness at the same time.
declared.falsifies_if: 10-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.6 'MACD crossover is faster but more falsy than MA crossover'

declared.rationale: note p.7: RSI<30 read as the conventional oversold / mean-reversion buy signal. Mechanics (horizon, exit, cap, stop) are identical to the prior study's oversold_bounce template, so this stream's five-symbol result is directly comparable to the prior study's QQQ/SOXX/IGV result, where it was a net loser on SOXX and IGV.
declared.falsifies_if: 5-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.7 RSI oversold/overbought reading

declared.rationale: note p.2: RSI framed as a 'trend strength regime' indicator rather than a reversion oscillator -- high RSI reads as confirmation of a strong trend worth joining, not exhaustion. Operationalized as a crossing event (entering a strong-momentum regime at 60) rather than a level, at the same horizon and direction as rsi_oversold_reversion so the two opposite readings of the same indicator can be compared head to head.
declared.falsifies_if: 10-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.2 RSI as trend-strength regime

declared.rationale: note p.2: 'price > 200MA = positive long term trend' implies the converse should be inferior. This is the direct mirror of trend-ma's regime_filter_standalone (close > sma(200)), not re-tested here -- see module docstring. direction='down' means the hypothesis under test is that the 20-bar forward hit rate is *below* the same-bars baseline while price sits under the 200-day SMA; an edge that runs positive is a rejection of that claim, not merely inconclusive.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate below the 200-day SMA does not fall below the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.2 'price > 200MA = positive long term trend' (converse)

declared.rationale: note p.2: 'trade only when broader market context is favorable', applied as a gate on a risk-managed entry (10% stop, 15-bar cap) rather than on a bare MA-alignment signal -- this is the risk-framework reading of the claim, not a crossover test. Paired with unfiltered_pullback (no gate) and unfavorable_regime_pullback (gate inverted) with every other parameter held fixed, so the marginal contribution of the regime gate on this class of trade can be read directly off the three edges.
declared.falsifies_if: 10-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline, or does not exceed unfiltered_pullback's edge
declared.source: note p.2 'trade only when broader market context is favorable'

declared.rationale: Identical to regime_filtered_pullback with the 'close > sma(200)' gate removed -- entry structure, exit, horizon, holding cap and stop all held fixed. The counterfactual that isolates whether the regime gate itself is doing work, not just whether rsi(14) < 30 mean-reversion works in general.
declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: regime-gate marginal-contribution probe, paired with regime_filtered_pullback

declared.rationale: The trade the note's risk framework discourages: buying an oversold bounce while price is already below the 200-day trend filter -- 'catching a falling knife' in a context the note itself calls unfavorable. direction is still declared 'up' (this idea asks whether the trade is a positive-edge trade on its own terms, not whether it under- or out-performs); the comparison against regime_filtered_pullback's edge and mechanics (win rate, max drawdown, worst trade) is what actually answers 'does the regime filter prevent catastrophic loss', in the report.
declared.falsifies_if: 10-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
declared.source: note p.2 risk framework: the trade explicitly discouraged by 'favorable context only'
